import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    p_values = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, col], feats.x[feats.y==0, col])
        p_values.append(p_val)
    
    # If all p-values > 0.05, claim no mechanism
    if all(p > 0.05 for p in p_values):
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select features with p < 0.05 and high effect size
    significant_features = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if p_values[i] < 0.05:
            col = feats.column(fid)
            effect_size = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, col]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, col])
            significant_features.append((fid, abs(effect_size), p_values[i]))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    significant_features.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlated with |r| >= 0.6)
    selected_features = []
    correlated_pairs = set()
    
    # Build correlations matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for fid, _, _ in significant_features:
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in selected_features:
            idx1 = feats.column(selected_fid)
            idx2 = feats.column(fid)
            if abs(corr_matrix[idx1, idx2]) >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected_features.append(fid)
            if len(selected_features) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # Fit logistic regression to get loadings
    if len(selected_features) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Use only selected features for regression
    X_selected = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_features]]
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_selected)
    
    # Fit logistic regression
    model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
    model.fit(X_scaled, feats.y)
    
    # Get coefficients
    weights = model.coef_[0]
    
    # Create loadings dictionary
    loadings = dict(zip(selected_features, weights))
    
    # For products, look for interactions between top features
    products = []
    top_features = selected_features[:min(3, len(selected_features))]
    
    # Add pairwise products of top features
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            products.append((top_features[i], top_features[j]))
    
    # Drivers are the top features by effect size
    drivers = tuple([fid for fid, _, _ in significant_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]])
    
    return Design(
        drivers=drivers,
        columns=tuple(selected_features),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
